public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 147

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/147](https://www.erdosproblems.com/147)
- [ErSi84] Erdős, P. and Simonovits, M., *Cube-supersaturated graphs and related problems*.
  Progress in graph theory (Waterloo, Ont., 1982) (1984), 203-218.
- [Er93] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favorite solved and unsolved problems in graph theory*.
  Quaestiones Math. (1993), 333-350.
- [Er97c] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favorite problems and results*. The mathematics of Paul Erdős,
  I (1997), 47-67.
- [Ja23] Janzer, Oliver, *Rainbow Turán number of even cycles, repeated patterns and blow-ups of
  cycles*. Israel J. Math. (2023), 813--840.
- [Ja23b] Janzer, Oliver, *Disproof of a conjecture of Erdős and Simonovits on the Turán number
  of graphs with minimum degree 3*. Int. Math. Res. Not. IMRN (2023), 8478--8494.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter Asymptotics SimpleGraph

namespace Erdos147

/--
If $H$ is bipartite with minimum degree $r$ then there exists $\epsilon=\epsilon(H)>0$ such that
$$\mathrm{ex}(n;H) \gg n^{2-\frac{1}{r-1}+\epsilon}.$$

Conjectured by Erdős and Simonovits [ErSi84]. A probabilistic argument shows that there exists
some $\epsilon=\epsilon(H)>0$ such that $\mathrm{ex}(n;H) \gg n^{2-\frac{2}{r}+\epsilon}$.

This conjecture was disproved by Janzer [Ja23] for even $r\geq 4$. The case $r=3$ was disproved
by Janzer [Ja23b], who constructed, for any $\epsilon>0$, a $3$-regular bipartite graph $H$ such
that $\mathrm{ex}(n;H)\ll n^{\frac{4}{3}+\epsilon}$.

In [Ja23] Janzer conjectures that the above lower bound is sharp, in that for any $r\geq 3$ and
$\epsilon>0$ there exists an $r$-regular graph $H$ such that
$\mathrm{ex}(n;H) \ll n^{2-\frac{2}{r}+\epsilon}$. Janzer's result proves this for even
$r\geq 4$.

See also [113](https://www.erdosproblems.com/113), [146](https://www.erdosproblems.com/146), and
[714](https://www.erdosproblems.com/714).

The conjecture is stated for minimum degree $r \geq 2$ (for $r = 1$ the exponent
$2 - \frac{1}{r-1}$ is not meaningful).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos147.lean#L799"]
theorem erdos_147 : answer(False) ↔
    ∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] [Nonempty V] (H : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel H.Adj],
      H.IsBipartite → 2 ≤ H.minDegree → ∃ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε ∧
        (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ) ^ (2 - 1 / ((H.minDegree : ℝ) - 1) + ε)) =O[atTop]
          fun n : ℕ => (extremalNumber n H : ℝ) := by
  sorry

open scoped Classical in
/--
Janzer [Ja23] disproved the conjecture for even $r\geq 4$: for any even $r \geq 4$ and
$\epsilon>0$ there exists an $r$-regular bipartite graph $H$ such that
$\mathrm{ex}(n;H) \ll n^{2-\frac{2}{r}+\epsilon}$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_147.variants.janzer_even (r : ℕ) (hr : 4 ≤ r) (heven : Even r) (ε : ℝ)
    (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∃ (q : ℕ) (H : SimpleGraph (Fin q)), H.IsBipartite ∧ H.IsRegularOfDegree r ∧
      (fun n : ℕ => (extremalNumber n H : ℝ)) =O[atTop]
        fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ) ^ (2 - 2 / (r : ℝ) + ε) := by
  sorry

open scoped Classical in
/--
Janzer [Ja23b] constructed, for any $\epsilon>0$, a $3$-regular bipartite graph $H$ such that
$\mathrm{ex}(n;H)\ll n^{\frac{4}{3}+\epsilon}$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_147.variants.cubic (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∃ (q : ℕ) (H : SimpleGraph (Fin q)), H.IsBipartite ∧ H.IsRegularOfDegree 3 ∧
      (fun n : ℕ => (extremalNumber n H : ℝ)) =O[atTop]
        fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ) ^ (4 / 3 + ε : ℝ) := by
  sorry

open scoped Classical in
/--
Janzer [Ja23] conjectures that for any $r\geq 3$ and $\epsilon>0$ there exists an $r$-regular
graph $H$ such that $\mathrm{ex}(n;H) \ll n^{2-\frac{2}{r}+\epsilon}$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_147.variants.janzer_conjecture : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ r : ℕ, 3 ≤ r → ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε →
    ∃ (q : ℕ) (H : SimpleGraph (Fin q)), H.IsRegularOfDegree r ∧
      (fun n : ℕ => (extremalNumber n H : ℝ)) =O[atTop]
        fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ) ^ (2 - 2 / (r : ℝ) + ε) := by
  sorry

end Erdos147

findings.description: The existential permits `q = 0`. With `H := (⊥ : SimpleGraph (Fin 0))`, bipartiteness holds and `H.IsRegularOfDegree r` is vacuous for every r. Moreover, the empty graph is contained in every host graph, so Mathlib's `extremalNumber n H` is 0 for every n (the supremum over an empty family of H-free graphs). Consequently this declaration holds with the same empty witness for every exponent, without using the degree, parity, or positivity hypotheses. It does not express Janzer's nonempty regular-graph construction. This witness and the exact stated conclusion were proved in `/workspace/review/scratch.lean`, without `sorryAx`.
findings.source_evidence: Janzer, [Ja23], arXiv:2006.01062v3, §1.3, Theorem 1.15, and §6: “For any even s and any δ>0, we have found an s-regular graph H (namely H=C_{2k}[s/2] for sufficiently large k)” with ex(n,H)=O(n^{2−2/s+δ}). These blown-up cycles have positive order. LaTeX source: https://arxiv.org/e-print/2006.01062.
findings.suggested_fix: Require a positive vertex count, for example `∃ (q : ℕ) (H : SimpleGraph (Fin q)), 0 < q ∧ H.IsBipartite ∧ H.IsRegularOfDegree r ∧ ...`, retaining the existing asymptotic bound.

findings.description: There is no nonemptiness requirement on the witness graph. Taking `q := 0` and `H := ⊥` makes `H.IsBipartite` true, `H.IsRegularOfDegree 3` vacuous, and `extremalNumber n H = 0` for all n. Thus the stated upper bound is trivial, even with any function replacing n^(4/3+ε). In particular, the witness need not have minimum degree 3 or provide the counterexample described by the source. A sorry-free proof of this exact variant using the empty witness is in `/workspace/review/scratch.lean`.
findings.source_evidence: Janzer, [Ja23b], arXiv:2109.06110v2, Theorem 1.4: “For any ε>0 there is a 3-regular (bipartite) graph H for which ex(n,H)=O(n^{4/3+ε}).” The following definition constructs H_{k,ℓ} on vertices x_{i,j}, 1≤i≤4k and 1≤j≤2ℓ, with k≥1 and ℓ≥2; these are nonempty graphs. The following lower-bound discussion also excludes a forbidden graph with identically zero extremal number. LaTeX source: https://arxiv.org/e-print/2109.06110.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `0 < q` as a conjunct in the existential conclusion, before the bipartiteness and regularity conditions.

findings.description: The entire right-hand side of `answer(sorry) ↔ ...` is trivially provable because its existential allows `q = 0`. The graph on `Fin 0` is regular of every degree, and its Mathlib extremal number is identically zero, hence is O(n^(2−2/r+ε)) for every r and ε. The answer slot therefore asks about a trivial empty-graph assertion rather than Janzer's conjecture about nonempty regular forbidden graphs. `/workspace/review/scratch.lean` proves the complete right-hand side with only standard Lean axioms.
findings.source_evidence: Janzer, [Ja23], arXiv:2006.01062v3, §6, conjectures that for odd s≥3 and every δ>0 there exists an s-regular graph H with ex(n,H)=O(n^{2−2/s+δ}), following the explicit nonempty constructions for even s. The next paragraph discusses the positive probabilistic lower bound for each fixed forbidden graph and the conjecture's sharpness. [Ja23b], arXiv:2109.06110v2, §3, repeats the conjecture and proves the s=3 case. Sources: https://arxiv.org/e-print/2006.01062 and https://arxiv.org/e-print/2109.06110.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the witness condition to `∃ (q : ℕ) (H : SimpleGraph (Fin q)), 0 < q ∧ H.IsRegularOfDegree r ∧ ...`. Keep the existing answer slot, quantifier order, and asymptotic bound.

sources_consulted: Oliver Janzer, Rainbow Turán number of even cycles, repeated patterns and blow-ups of cycles, arXiv:2006.01062v3, especially §§1.3 and 6; https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.01062 and https://arxiv.org/e-print/2006.01062.

Oliver Janzer, Disproof of a conjecture of Erdős and Simonovits on the Turán number of graphs with minimum degree 3, arXiv:2109.06110v2, especially Theorem 1.4 and §3; https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.06110 and https://arxiv.org/e-print/2109.06110.
Erdős and Simonovits, Cube-supersaturated graphs and related problems (1984), https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1984-04.pdf.
Crossref bibliographic records for [Er93], DOI 10.1080/16073606.1993.9631741, and [Er97c], DOI 10.1007/978-3-642-60408-9_3; full texts were not obtained.
The linked proof's custom dependencies at the same commit: ErdosProblems/Erdos147/Basic.lean, Core.lean, Conflict.lean, Regularization.lean, and ErdosProblems/Erdos888/ColoredGraph.lean.

Local Mathlib sources: Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/Finite.lean, Copy.lean, Bipartite.lean, Coloring/Vertex.lean, Extremal/Basic.lean; Analysis/Asymptotics/Defs.lean and Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/Real.lean.
review.notes: All three findings are the same missing nonemptiness condition in separate declarations. The scratch proofs establish the stronger assertion that an empty witness works for every degree and every real-valued upper-bound function. The main theorem has no identified defect: its minimum-degree restriction excludes the bad boundary cases, its Big-O direction expresses the intended lower bound, and its fixed negative answer agrees with the literature and current status data. I compiled the linked proof and its custom dependencies, then derived the exact main statement in `/workspace/review/external-proof.lean`; both axiom checks contain only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. Extending Janzer's odd-degree conjecture to all r≥3 is not an additional defect, since the even cases are established. Direct access to erdosproblems.com/147 remained blocked by Cloudflare, so its latest remarks could not be read; the declarations' mathematical content was checked against the primary Janzer papers.

demonstrated.claim: The exact statement is provable using q = 0, whose empty graph is bipartite, regular of every degree, and has identically zero extremal number.
The exact statement is provable using q = 0 because cubic regularity is vacuous and the extremal-number upper bound reduces to a bound on zero.
The exact imported statement is trivially provable because q = 0 witnesses its existential conclusion for every r and ε.

submission.summary: Created /workspace/review/trivial_proof.lean with short proofs of all three exact declaration types using type_of%. The requested compilation reports no errors or warnings, and all three axiom checks contain only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound.

trivial_proof.lean:
import FormalConjectures.ErdosProblems.«147»

/-!
All three existence variants admit `q = 0`: the graph on `Fin 0` is regular of
any degree, and its extremal number is zero, so every upper bound is satisfied.
The proofs below use the declarations' exact types, not their imported proofs.
-/

open Filter Asymptotics
open scoped Classical

namespace Review147Trivial

-- Every host graph contains the empty graph, so there are no empty-graph-free hosts.
private lemma empty_extremal (n : ℕ) :
    SimpleGraph.extremalNumber n (⊥ : SimpleGraph (Fin 0)) = 0 := by
  apply Nat.eq_zero_of_le_zero
  rw [← Fintype.card_fin n, SimpleGraph.extremalNumber_le_iff]
  intro G _ hfree
  exact (hfree SimpleGraph.IsContained.of_isEmpty).elim

-- Thus the same empty graph satisfies an upper bound by ANY function, not just a power.
private lemma empty_bigO (f : ℕ → ℝ) :
    (fun n : ℕ => (SimpleGraph.extremalNumber n (⊥ : SimpleGraph (Fin 0)) : ℝ))
      =O[atTop] f := by
  simp only [empty_extremal, Nat.cast_zero]
  exact Asymptotics.isBigO_zero _ _

-- Erdos147.erdos_147.variants.janzer_even:
-- Provable with q = 0, without using the degree, parity, or positivity hypotheses.
theorem janzer_even_trivial : type_of% @Erdos147.erdos_147.variants.janzer_even := by
  intro r _ _ ε _
  exact ⟨0, ⊥, ⟨SimpleGraph.Coloring.ofIsEmpty⟩,
    SimpleGraph.IsRegularOfDegree.of_isEmpty, empty_bigO _⟩

-- Erdos147.erdos_147.variants.cubic:
-- Provable with q = 0: even cubic regularity is vacuous on the empty vertex type.
theorem cubic_trivial : type_of% @Erdos147.erdos_147.variants.cubic := by
  intro ε _
  exact ⟨0, ⊥, ⟨SimpleGraph.Coloring.ofIsEmpty⟩,
    SimpleGraph.IsRegularOfDegree.of_isEmpty, empty_bigO _⟩

-- Erdos147.erdos_147.variants.janzer_conjecture:
-- The open conjecture's entire right-hand side is provable by taking q = 0 for every r and ε.
theorem janzer_conjecture_trivial :
    type_of% @Erdos147.erdos_147.variants.janzer_conjecture := by
  refine ⟨fun _ r _ ε _ => ?_, fun _ => True.intro⟩
  exact ⟨0, ⊥, SimpleGraph.IsRegularOfDegree.of_isEmpty, empty_bigO _⟩

#print axioms janzer_even_trivial
#print axioms cubic_trivial
#print axioms janzer_conjecture_trivial

end Review147Trivial

submission.summary: Added `0 < q` to all three existential conclusions, excluding the empty-graph witnesses, and clarified nonemptiness in their docstrings. The main theorem, asymptotic bounds, answer slot, and attributes are unchanged. The requested compilation succeeds with only the existing `declaration uses 'sorry'` warnings.
